key_insight: Discrete suction through perforated rows can delay Blasius boundary-layer transition, with an optimal suction level beyond which the transition front moves upstream again.
engineering_relevance: Because suction volume flow rate, not suction velocity, best predicts the effect, the findings help guide practical boundary-layer control design using manufacturable perforations.
method: Applied suction through discrete hole rows in a Blasius boundary layer.
Varied displacement-thickness Reynolds number at suction from 1400 to 1600.
Compared configurations with 4 vs 10 rows and assessed intermittency and velocity spectra from hot-wire anemometry.
evidence_signal: Hot-wire measurements of intermittency and streamwise-velocity spectra showed downstream transition shift at increasing suction, followed by upstream movement when suction exceeded the optimum.
watch_item: The optimum appears sensitive to operating Reynolds number and suction flow rate, so results may not transfer directly without re-tuning the perforation layout and suction strength.
paper_title: Study of discrete boundary layer suction for transition delay
